note: First run. Written by Claude from web research; check details before booking.

items.title: Ben Howard at People Festival
items.summary: His only listed date right now, and the last stop of the current run. A two-day festival in the old East German broadcasting house on the Spree.

items.title: Under One Sky: 400 years of Japanese art
items.summary: Deities, people and animals in Japanese art, shown in Ando's concrete-and-glass building on the former missile base at Insel Hombroich. About 2.5 hours from Den Haag.
items.why: Ando architecture, Japanese art, art in landscape

items.title: Sabine Marcelis: Continuum
items.summary: The Rotterdam designer's intervention in Rem Koolhaas's building itself: light, colour and material working with the architecture.
items.why: Light and space, art with architecture

items.title: Benedikte Bjerre: When the wind blows
items.summary: A playful, interactive installation of helium-filled sculptures that drift and gather. Combine with Continuum in one visit.

items.title: Base Line
items.summary: Thematic show in Berlage's building. Worth pairing with the Mondrian rooms on a rainy, windless day.

items.title: Silent mornings at Voorlinden
items.summary: Every Saturday and Sunday morning the museum runs a silent visit. Turrell's Skyspace in the dunes is part of the permanent collection.

items.title: Tokyo Atlas
items.summary: International outdoor exhibition placing contemporary art in waterfront parks and public space, including monumental installations.

items.title: Invisible Garden
items.summary: Embroidered landscapes and transparent cell-like sculptures that shimmer and dissolve as you move. Small, quiet, free.

items.title: Roppongi Art Night
items.summary: One all-night festival of light and large-scale installations across the district.

items.title: Rokko Meets Art
items.summary: Contemporary art spread through the forest and viewpoints on Mt Rokko. Closest thing to the Murou Art Forest feeling near Osaka.

items.title: Happy Food & Health
items.summary: 100% gluten-free kitchen with vegan dishes, so dairy- and egg-free choices are easy. Ask about oats.

items.title: Sabor Sabor
items.summary: Latin cantina with an open kitchen where the whole menu is gluten-free. Not dairy-free by default, so ask which dishes skip cheese and cream.

items.title: The SUE Store
items.summary: Everything is gluten-free and vegan, so no dairy or eggs. Brunch-style menu; plant milks may include oat, so ask for another.

items.title: Mammamia
items.summary: Rated 4.7, praised by coeliac guests for its gluten-free pizza. Cheese is standard, so order without and check the dough for egg.

items.title: THE SECONDROOM
items.summary: Rated 4.6. Fully vegan and gluten-free, so okonomiyaki, takoyaki and gyoza are all safe from gluten, dairy and egg. Closed Wednesdays.

items.title: Buddha (gluten-free & vegan)
items.summary: Rated 4.7. Gluten-free and vegan, and guests with dairy and egg allergies say they felt safe. Bowls, soups, tacos. Lunch only, closed Sundays.

items.title: FOLK cafe + bakery
items.summary: Rated 5.0. Vegan bakery-café with gluten-free options and a seasonal menu. Not all of it is gluten-free, so ask which bakes are.

items.title: Dune: Part Three in cinemas
items.summary: Denis Villeneuve, who made Arrival, closes his Dune trilogy with Dune Messiah. Worth an IMAX screen.

items.title: Pick: Perfect Days (Wim Wenders, 2023)
items.summary: A Tokyo toilet cleaner's quiet, repeated days, shot like a meditation. Especially good while you're in Japan.

items.title: Pick: The Ministry for the Future (Kim Stanley Robinson)
items.summary: Idea-driven science fiction where the plot is climate finance and adaptation: carbon coins, central banks, heat waves. Chiang-level thinking, aimed at your day job.

items.title: Pick: The Mountain Shadow (Gregory David Roberts)
items.summary: The sequel to Shantaram: Lin back in Bombay two years later, heavier on philosophy. If you haven't read it yet.

items.title: Pick: The Dispossessed (Ursula K. Le Guin)
items.summary: A physicist moves between two worlds and two economic systems. Like Chiang, it is really about how an idea reshapes a life.

items.title: Pick: Wheels of Life (Anodea Judith)
items.summary: The practical companion to Eastern Body, Western Mind: the chakra system as an embodied practice rather than theory.

items.title: 2-day Zen meditation retreat, Shunkō-in
items.summary: In English with the temple's priest. The Oct 29–30 retreat is sold out; Oct 2–3 and Nov 13–14 are still listed. Shorter 2-hour zen-and-tea sessions run most mornings.

items.title: Zen silent retreat, autumn
items.summary: Four-day silent zen retreat. I couldn't open the page to confirm location and price, so check before booking.

items.title: Silent museum mornings, Voorlinden
items.summary: Weekend mornings in silence, including Turrell's Skyspace. Meditation and museum in one.

items.title: EIC Accelerator: Deep Tech for Climate Adaptation
items.summary: 2026 challenge for startups on urban heat, climate-smart agriculture, water scarcity, and flood and coastal protection. Useful for startups you work with; cut-off dates are in the Work Programme.

items.title: Climate-ADAPT events calendar
items.summary: The EU's running list of adaptation conferences and webinars. Radar checks it for finance-relevant sessions in NL and Brussels.

items.title: Autumn food in Japan: chestnuts and new rice
items.summary: Kuri gohan (chestnut rice), roasted sweet potato and shinmai (new-crop rice) are naturally gluten-, dairy- and egg-free. Watch the soy sauce: regular shoyu contains wheat, so ask for tamari.
